newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares pick up on month-end orders.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares pick up on month-end orders.

text.p: Danish share prices, weakened since Wednesday's hints of a possible U.S. rate rise in remarks by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan, got a boost from late orders on Friday but dealers doubted that the rise would continue next week.

"The market was weak from the start but month-end orders at the end of the day pushed the KFX index up. But buying interest is generally low for now and if it doesn't improve the market could well fall again on Monday," a chief trader said.
The KFX top-20 index gained 0.24 point to 152.97 in overall bourse turnover of 1.05 billion crowns.
Its March future rose 0.20 point to 152.97 with 423 contracts, each worth 100,000 crowns, traded.

ISS, which said that its Vice-President was quitting over differences with other directors, was the day's most-traded share but ended with its price unchanged at 185 crowns. Dealers said the news could dent the share on Monday.

Shipping group A.P.Moeller's DS Svendborg and DS 1912 shares rose respectively by 2,767.5 crowns to 267,767.5 and by 2,000 crowns to 186,000. The company is seen as a possible beneficiary of U.S. attempts to win Japanese port concessions on container handling.
